text:
alex: Heads up — onboarding demo (local) hammered our staging quota with tons of 429s. Saw a few responses that had Retry-After but client retried immediately.
rachel: Ugh. Which SDK and which flow?
alex: JS SDK, pagination for embeddings. The runner forks multiple page fetches concurrently (default 32). When a 429 arrives with Retry-After: 3, the SDK still retries per its exponential backoff instead of honoring the header.
tony: I remember we intentionally added generic backoff in the transport layer, but didn't plumb Retry-After. That's parity gap vs Python.
alex: Right. Python checks Retry-After and sets sleep accordingly. JS just increments backoff multiplier. Result: clobbered token quotas and noisy metrics.
ci-bot: test-suite: sdk-js/retry-after-handling failed on CI (integration test simulated 429+Retry-After).
rachel: Can we patch the JS transport quickly? Minimal change: if Retry-After present and parseable, use that value as base delay before next attempt.
tony: Agreed. Also propose we add client-side throttling to the sample runner. 32 concurrent pagination requests is too aggressive for newcomers. Could add a concurrency default of 6 and optional flag `--max-parallel`.
alex: I'd rather a token-bucket qps limiter + concurrency semaphore. That prevents bursts and smooths sustained traffic. Simple API: `RateGate(qps=10, burst=20)` and `Semaphore(n)`.
rachel: Good idea. For immediate fix I'll open a tiny PR that reads Retry-After in fetch wrapper and uses Math.max(currentBackoff, retryAfterMs). Tests included.
tony: For medium-term, let's add an adaptive limiter in the JS SDK that reduces concurrency on repeated 429s from the server. Basic heuristic: on N 429s within M seconds reduce concurrency by half, then ramp back slowly.
alex: We should also change the sample-app to stream pages and checkpoint the cursor to disk so retries don't re-fetch already processed pages. Right now it holds everything in memory and restarts work on failure.
ci-bot: deploy: sample-runner v0.4.0 -> staging queued.
ops-bot: quota alert: staging project tokens nearing burst limit (1m tokens used in last 10m).
rachel: For observability: emit metric tags `retry_policy=header|backoff`, `retry_after_ms`, `retry_count`, and `effective_concurrency`. Console can surface a small chart.
tony: Also add a small devex doc snippet: minimal client-side throttling patterns for Node and Python. Include code examples for token-bucket and async iterator pagination. Keep them copy-paste ready.
alex: I'll draft the doc and a sample CLI flag `--auto-backoff` default false (so behavior is opt-in until we validate).
ci-bot: branch tests: alex/sdk-retry-after + rachel/samplerateflags passed.
rachel: Merged the quick fix for Retry-After into main. Can we schedule a follow-up to wire adaptive limiter and sample-runner changes into the quickstart? New users keep hitting this during the free credits onboarding.
tony: I'll own the adaptive limiter RFC and put a prototype in the js-sdk/examples dir. alex, can you drop the checkpointing pattern into the sample runner PR?
alex: Yep, will PR today. Also adding e2e that simulates Retry-After headers and asserts the client waits the right ms and doesn't exceed configured qps.
rachel: Thanks — feel better about this. Small set of changes should reduce 429 noise and smooth onboarding. :thumbsup:
